activity_summary: At the door, before you crossed, Heminges had my lord's leave for the jig and no purse with it. Phillips told Nick to come in under the note. Nick said he was glad, and he did not sing in the yard. You kept the tale as it is, and you said a lost roll would get your hands before your nerves did. The two cloaks stayed at the inn for tomorrow's count.

entities.name: William Shakespeare
entities.context: Kept the play once, and offered your hands to a lost roll rather than to your nerves.

entities.name: John Heminges
entities.context: Brought the leave, and entered nothing.

entities.name: Augustine Phillips
entities.context: Set Nick under the note and kept the gladness off the pitch.

entities.name: Nick Sorrell
entities.context: Said he was glad, and did not sing the verse in the yard.

entities.name: Will Kemp
entities.context: Took the jig as feet, not as a new play.

entities.name: Arthur Meeks
entities.context: Knew his beat, and refused a speech about it.

entities.name: Richard Burbage
entities.context: Kept you off a rehearsal of fear, and kept Sam off the floor.

entities.name: George Bryan
entities.context: In the yard, and did not add a condition.

entities.name: Henry Carey, 1st Lord Hunsdon
entities.context: Not in the yard. His leave came by a man at the door.

facets.activity: Heard my lord's leave for the jig

quotes.speaker: john_heminges
quotes.text: A man at the door brought my lord's leave for the jig.

quotes.speaker: augustine_phillips
quotes.text: Leave is not a pitch. Glad is not a pitch.

quotes.speaker: nick_sorrell
quotes.text: I have a verse. I am glad of it.

quotes.speaker: william_shakespeare
quotes.text: The old play, once. Then your job.
